newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks Russian aid for reactor upgrading.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks Russian aid for reactor upgrading.

text.p: Bulgaria is seeking funding from Russia for the upgrading of its Soviet-made nuclear power plant and eventual completion of a second nuclear power station, Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov said.

"The draft co-operation agreement that we will offer for signing to our Russian colleagues envisages that Russia should extend to Bulgaria a credit of up to $250 million," state news agency BTA quoted Ovcharov as saying.

"The credit will be used for the upgrading and modernisation of the four 440-megawatt nuclear reactors at Kozloduy nuclear power plant and for our joint work at the Belene nuclear power plant," Ovcharov told reporters.
The construction of Bulgaria's second nuclear plant at Belene was halted in 1990 due to lack of cash and environmental protests.
The Kozloduy plant, which also has two more modern 1,000- megawatt reactors, produces more than 40 percent of Bulgaria's electricity.
Russia is expected to answer Bulgaria's offer within several weeks and an agreement for nuclear energy cooperation should be signed in January next year, BTA said.
Heavily-indebted Bulgaria has suggested payment in goods and construction services rather than cash.

The nuclear plant at Kozloduy, and particularly its oldest reactors number one and two, have long been at the centre of international concern over their safety. A mission of the International Atomic Agency recommended their closure in 1991.
The reactors were restarted in 1992 and 1993 respectively but were closed periodically for further repairs.
Kozloduy plans to complete the safety reconstruction programme of its four reactors in 1997 and has already invested 2.2 billion levs in it.
In 1993 wealthy European countries through the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development donated 24 million Ecus for equipment for reactors three and four.
